routes.label: Find the rotation angle by cosine

question: Riders on a Ferris wheel travel in a circle in a vertical plane. A particular wheel has radius \(20\) feet and revolves at the constant rate of one revolution per minute. How many seconds does it take a rider to travel from the bottom of the wheel to a point \(10\) vertical feet above the bottom?
solution:
At a constant rotation rate, time is proportional to the angle turned. We first find the angle needed to reach the specified height.

Let \(O\) be the center, \(B\) the bottom point, and \(P\) a point on the wheel \(10\) feet above \(B\). Let the horizontal line through \(P\) meet \(OB\) at \(H\). Since \(OB=20\), we have \(BH=OH=10\). Thus \(PH\) is the perpendicular bisector of \(OB\).

A point on a perpendicular bisector is equally distant from the segment’s endpoints, so \(PO=PB\). Also, \(PO=OB=20\), since both are radii. Hence all three sides of \(\triangle OPB\) are equal, giving
\[
\angle BOP=60^\circ.
\]
The two points at this height lie on opposite sides of the vertical diameter. In either direction, the rider first reaches one after turning \(60^\circ\), or one sixth of a revolution. A full revolution takes \(60\) seconds, so the time is
\[
\frac16\cdot60=\boxed{10\text{ seconds}},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
